# Issue #309 RE2-authority screen differential corpus (curated half).
# Hand-written: ordinary matcher shapes plus every construct where the Rust
# `regex` crate's accepted grammar is known or suspected to differ from
# RE2's. One pattern per line, verbatim (no escaping layer); `#` and blank
# lines are prose. Replayed against a real RE2 by
# tests/re2_screen_differential.rs.
.*
.+
.

(?P<n>a)
(?<n>a)
(?P<n.x>a)
(?#c)a

# Issue #317 — constructs BOTH engines accept and read differently (value
# divergences, not status ones). The rewrite in pulsus-promql::re2_syntax
# gives the Rust crate RE2's reading; these are what proves it.
\d
\D
\w
\W
\s
\S
\d+
\w+\s*

# Issue #324 — `.` versus newline. ClickHouse's `match()` compiles with
# RE2's `dot_nl` option set, so `.` matched a line break there and does not
# in RE2 itself. These are the shapes that separate the two readings, plus
# the `s` flag the user may still set deliberately and the negated classes
# that must keep their own (correct) newline behaviour.
.
.*
.+
a.b
a.*b
^.$
(?s).
(?s).*
(?s:.)
(?s:a.b)
(?s)a.b
a(?s).b
(?i)a.b
(?s)(?i).
[^a]
[^\n]
[^a\n]
\n
a\nb
.\n.
(.|\n)
(?:.|\n)*
\s
\S
[[:space:]]
[^[:space:]]
.{2}
.{1,3}
(?s).{2}
\.
a\.b
